4c6e45453255: Start with a question to the group: “How many of you are in your family? How many friends will come to the birthday party?” Let the students try to answer in Polish, then show that Polish has different numerals for men and for a mixed group.
beba8b17d577: This is the key idea of the whole lesson: in Polish, men have their own numeral. Ask the check question “are they all men?” — we will come back to it on every slide.
a24945d5dbbc: Reveal row by row. Stress that in the masculine row the forms for 5 and 10 are different too (pięciu, dziesięciu), not only for 2–4. Ask the students to read the row aloud.
48fdffe74bd2: Abbreviations: M. — mianownik, B. — biernik, D. — dopełniacz, C. — celownik, N. — narzędnik, Msc. — miejscownik. Key points: for men the accusative equals the genitive (widzę trzech kolegów). Different forms only in C. and N.
dbbea433a5d2: Show that after a numeral the noun stands in dopełniacz liczby mnogiej (genitive plural), and the verb is usually neuter singular: przyszło. Don't go into the variants — they are in the exceptions block.
0e87647c897c: Compare men and animals: trzech kolegów, but trzy psy. Animals are counted like things. This prepares the trap about koty.
fb888fd79982: The ending -u in all cases except the instrumental (-oma). Add jedenastu, dwunastu, trzynastu orally — they are formed the same way. Don't demand the instrumental from a weaker group.
baca6eff1ce9: The question word ilu is used only for men. For «how many people» we say ile osób. Ask the students to put the question to their partner: Ilu masz kolegów?
6ce084d44b3f: The second half of the topic: collective numerals. If the group has both men and women, or it is children, we say dwoje, troje, czworo. Ask the students: “A boy and a girl — how many is that?”
c36af2545f93: Do not demand all cases from the weaker group: the main ones are M./B. (nominative/accusative: dwoje dzieci) and D. (genitive: dla dwojga dzieci). The instrumental (z trojgiem dzieci) is for stronger students. Note that 4 is czworo, not “czteroro”.
53efcbcefb54: The formula is the same as for men: numeral + noun in the genitive plural + verb in the neuter. The only difference is in the numeral itself.
09df3e2439ee: Three typical cases: children, a mixed group, and «ludzie» without specifying gender. Ask the students to make up their own sentence about their family: Mam troje rodzeństwa.
587f86220539: Osoba is feminine, so in the mianownik (nominative) we say trzy osoby, pięć osób, even when we are talking about men. In the biernik (accusative) and after prepositions the numeral changes: dla pięciu osób, z pięcioma osobami.
38b58cde6390: The construction «było nas troje» is very lively in conversation. Show the pair: było nas troje (mixed group) and było ich czterech (all men). Ask a few students to say how many of them were at the last party.
4e003e472bf6: Dwaj, trzej, czterej — only in the nominative and only in bookish language; in speech we say dwóch. Ludzie allows both forms: pięciu ludzi (men) and pięcioro ludzi (mixed group).
42e22e9f7cf9: Three cases: 4 gives czworo (not czteroro), young animals (szczenięta, kocięta) are counted with collective numerals, and plural-only nouns (drzwi) too. For drzwi you can also say dwie pary drzwi.
516a4e476aba: The first trap is a literal translation of “two boys”. The second — “five people”. The third — “there were three of us” with the wrong trzy. Ask students why they are so prone to these mistakes.
4a47f3ed9092: Three typical case and gender mistakes here: narzędnik (instrumental) after z, osoba in the nominative, hypercorrection with animals. Ask students to correct the «wrong» themselves before the ✓ is revealed.
